The cost of operational friction

Most regulatory risk starts in ordinary operations

The problems regulators find are rarely dramatic. They are the accumulated result of processes that depend on workarounds, individuals and unrecorded decisions.

  • 01

    Critical processes hidden in spreadsheets

    The logic lives in one person’s head and one unversioned workbook. When that person leaves, the control leaves with them.

  • 02

    Investigations tracked through email

    Evidence is scattered across inboxes with no single record of who decided what, and when.

  • 03

    Manual evidence collection

    Analysts rebuild the same evidence pack for every review cycle, at the cost of time that should go to judgement.

  • 04

    Reporting assembled by hand

    Regulatory returns are compiled in the final days and reconciled by eye, which is where errors enter.

  • 05

    Disconnected systems

    Re-keying between tools creates discrepancies that tend to surface only during an audit or examination.

  • 06

    Lack of audit trails

    Decisions cannot be reconstructed, so every examination becomes an expensive reconstruction exercise.

  • 07

    AI experiments without governance

    Models and copilots are trialled in isolation, with no owner, no approval route and no evidence trail.

What makes Zi Cloud different

Automation that your regulator can follow

Most automation firms are judged by the tasks they remove. We are judged by whether the control still works afterwards.

Typical automation firm

  • Automates tasks in isolation
  • Leads with the technology
  • Limited focus on governance and control design
  • Measures success by tasks removed

Zi Cloud

  • Designs controlled workflows end to end
  • Builds auditability into every process
  • Enables AI within defined risk boundaries
  • Understands regulated environments and their supervisors
  • Balances automation with human oversight
  • Measures success by control quality and cycle time

How we work

One programme, from process to proof

We do not hand over a set of automations and leave. We design the control, build the workflow and leave your team able to operate it.

Stage 1

Discovery

A fixed-scope diagnostic of one or more processes, producing a validated current state and prioritised opportunities.

Stage 2

Design

Target workflows, control mapping, architecture and governance, designed with the people who will operate them.

Stage 3

Build and Deliver

Controlled build in staged releases, with testing against the control requirements and handover to your team.

Stage 4

Assure

Independent review at key gates, so go-live decisions rest on tested evidence rather than confidence.

Our principles

Governance first, not governance last

Governance first

Controls are designed before automation is built, so nothing goes live that second line cannot test.

Human oversight by design

People remain accountable for consequential decisions. Automation handles volume, not judgement.

Auditability as a requirement

Every automated step, AI output and human approval leaves a record that can be reconstructed later.

Workflow is the asset

The process design is what you own. Tools change, and a well-designed workflow survives the change.

About the founder

A practitioner who has designed and delivered operational change

Asif is a practitioner who has designed and delivered large-scale operational change inside major financial institutions. Zi Cloud exists because the gap he saw repeatedly was not a lack of technology. It was a lack of workflow design that could hold up to regulatory scrutiny.

Asif’s career has spanned banking, financial crime operations, regulatory reporting, data transformation and operational transformation. Across those areas, the same pattern recurred: processes that worked on the day they were designed and then drifted, controls that existed on paper and not in practice, and automation that solved a local problem while creating a new governance one.
